source_text: Scio quoniam conabuntur quidam etiam secundum scripturas nostras dicere deum corpus esse, quoniam inveniunt scriptum esse apud Moysen quidem: "Deus noster ignis consumens est", in evangelio vero secundum Iohannem: "Deus spiritus est, et eos qui adorant eum, in spiritu et veritate oportet adorare". Ignis vero et spiritus non aliud apud eos quam corpus esse putabitur. Quos interrogare volo, quid dicant de eo quod scriptum est, quia "deus lux est", sicut Iohannes in epistola sua dicit: "Deus lux est, et tenebrae non sunt in eo". Ista nempe lux est, quae inluminat omnem sensum eorum, qui possunt capere veritatem, sicut in tricesimo quinto psalmo dicitur: "In lumine tuo videbimus lumen". Quid enim aliud lumen dei dicendum est, in quo quis videt lumen, nisi virtus dei, per quam quis inluminatus vel veritatem rerum omnium pervidet vel ipsum deum cognoscit, qui veritas appellatur? Tale est ergo quod dicitur: "In lumine tuo videbimus lumen", hoc est, in verbo tuo et sapientia tua, qui est filius tuus, in ipso te videbimus patrem. Numquidnam quia lumen nominatur, simile putabitur solis huius lumini?
pass_a_gloss: I know that some will try even according to our scriptures to say God is a body, because they find written in Moses our God is a consuming fire and in the gospel according to John God is spirit; I ask what they say of God is light.
pass_b_english: I know some will try from our Scriptures to say God is a body, finding in Moses [[our God is a consuming fire >> Bible:Deuteronomy 4:24]] and in John [[God is spirit >> Bible:John 4:24]]. Fire and spirit they take as nothing but body. Ask them what they say of [[God is light, and in him is no darkness >> Bible:1 John 1:5]]. That light is what illumines every mind that can receive truth, as the psalm says [[in your light we see light >> Bible:Psalm 36:9]] — that is, in your Word and Wisdom, your Son, we see you the Father. The name “light” does not make him like this sun’s bodily light.
notes: Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
